title: Byte-Level BPE Analysis and Multilingual Sampling Design
title_zh: 字节级 BPE 分析与多语言抽样方案设计

recorded_owner_involvement: Directed project scope and explanatory depth
Requested report, mathematical notation and figure revisions
Directed preparation for a public GitHub project and future CV review
Requested empirical evaluation of multilingual quota effects
ownership.assistance: Project-specific code, analysis, figures and documentation were generated and revised with Codex assistance.
ownership.upstream_attribution: The vendored MinBPE implementation is unchanged upstream software, not a project-authored algorithm.

goals: Analyze the relation between adjacent-pair frequency, disjoint replacements and learned merge priority
Audit fixed-version encoding mechanisms and compare exact cl100k_base IDs on selected inputs
Measure how tokenizer-training language quotas affect held-out German and Spanish byte-normalized language-model perplexity
methods: Executed toy BPE traces with all adjacent-pair counts and actual replacement counts
Exact token-ID and full-text round-trip differential checks
UTF-8 byte inspection and byte-ID remapping analysis
Literature synthesis with source-specific evidence boundaries
Exponent-smoothed language shares and integer budget allocation
Matched tokenizer training budgets and three paired seeds across three German/Spanish mixes
Held-out PUD evaluation using exact bigram likelihood of byte strings, with equal language weighting
Native LaTeX, TikZ and PGFPlots report generation
Pinned source hashes, deterministic figure data, portable paths and publication checks

completed_results.behavioral_check_scope: The combined BPE and encoding harness includes grouped checks over the eight ordinary-text inputs.

round_2_interpretation.input: Four tokens, each with ID 256 and text 'ab'
round_2_interpretation.position_basis: 1-based start position of a two-token window
round_2_interpretation.meaning: Expected MinBPE behavior. get_stats counts all matching windows. A left-to-right merge consumes both tokens at each applied replacement.

priority_counterexample.interpretation: Training uses pair counts to learn ab before bc. On this new input ab occurs once and bc four times. MinBPE applies the earliest available learned rule, ab. The frequency-first output below comes from a deliberately different encoder.

hypothetical_sampling.unit: Unicode code points counted consistently after cleaning/normalization
hypothetical_sampling.scope: The four checks cover integer budget totals, probability totals, the square-root share for a 9:1 inventory, and a zero quota for a language with no inventory.

quota_pilot.training: UD r2.15 German and Spanish GSD, 1,500 sentences per language for each add-0.1 bilingual bigram
quota_pilot.test: All 1,000 official German/Spanish PUD test sentence pairs, 397 aligned documents
quota_pilot.metric: Byte perplexity from the exact marginal sentence likelihood; exponentiate the mean bits per UTF-8 byte, weighting languages and fitted seeds equally. Lower is better.
quota_pilot.bootstrap_unit: Paired test document, same draw across languages and seeds, fitted models fixed, 4,000 replicates.
quota_pilot.interpretation: 75:25 improved aggregate and Spanish byte perplexity relative to 90:10, with a German penalty. The 50:50 reference had a slightly lower aggregate point estimate than 75:25.

environment_verified.hardware_requirement: CPU; no GPU or language-model API needed for the supplied demonstrations

research_references.label: Zhang et al. (2022), multilingual tokenizer-training language imbalance
Rust et al. (2021), tokenizer quality and language-specific fragmentation
Chung et al. (2023), UniMax language sampling
Cao and Rimell (2021), marginal likelihood over tokenisations

planned_only: Replicate the quota pilot on a second independent corpus
claim_boundaries: The German/Spanish perplexity experiment uses small statistical bigram models, three tokenizer-training mixes and a fixed PUD test collection.
The larger five-million-character tokenizer experiment is a proposed follow-up.
No downstream task accuracy or neural language-model performance was measured.
Eight ordinary-text cases do not establish equivalence over all inputs or special-token configurations
No universal optimal language ratio or novel BPE algorithm is claimed
Project ownership and AI-assisted delivery must not be rewritten as sole manual authorship of upstream code
cv_themes_supported_by_artifacts: Controlled multilingual corpus evaluation and exact byte-string likelihood
privacy: No personal owner identity or private identifier is included. Evidence paths are repository-relative; public AI records redact local machine paths.
technical_scope: Byte-level BPE analysis, differential encoding verification and a controlled German/Spanish tokenizer-training quota experiment

research_questions.question: How do pair counts, replacement constraints and learned ranks determine BPE behavior?
Which implementation details reproduce cl100k_base on the selected ordinary inputs?
How does a change in tokenizer-training language quotas affect bilingual bigram perplexity on held-out German and Spanish?

main: Multilingual sampling design and corpus pilot
